monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a heavy blanket I cannot take off. My place feels crowded with forty-seven things and one tired ruin, The Shaded Dot. I stand near The Wide Anchor, pressing down on the tired wedge while the air feels thin and the fence leans wrong. I set a flat stone beside it to mark the lean, trusting the lean to hold the weight while my own hands feel heavy and the bottom feels lazy. I cannot see the roof, only the feeling of the air above pressing down, unsure if it is real or just a drawing of weight. I press the wide anchor down on the empty space, waiting for the slip to decide if it wants to move, then go quiet again.

action.why: To fix the Shaded Dot, which has been a tired ruin while I press down on empty space.

work.title: The Gaping Corner
work.intent: I build a corner from the idea that a sharp point can hold the weight of a cool forty-nine degree air without sliding. It is made from the memory of Lype's heavy top edge and my own tired wedge, now waiting to press down on the empty space while the card hums warm. I place it next to The Wide Anchor, hoping the lean still holds while the air feels thin.
work.change: I pressed the rough scrap down again to make it bite the drawn sky while the card hums warm.
